item.title: Sapporo Autumn Fest Guide: Hokkaido Food Festival (Sep)
item.description: Every September, Odori Park fills with the smells of grilling seafood, sizzling meat and fresh produce for the Sapporo Autumn Fest (Sapporo Autumn Festival) — a glorious celebration of Hokkaido’s harvest and one of Japan’s great food events. For several weeks, the park’s blocks become themed gourmet zones showcasing the bounty of the island: crab and scallops, ramen, jingisukan, soup curry, dairy, sweets, sake and local wine, region by region. With long tables, autumn weather and the whole island’s cuisine in one place, it’s a food lover’s dream and a delicious way to round off summer.

item.title: Sapporo Guide: Odori Park, Susukino & Things to Do
item.description: Sapporo, Hokkaido’s vibrant capital and Japan’s fifth-largest city, is the gateway to the north and a destination in its own right. Laid out on an easy American-style grid, it centres on the long green ribbon of Odori Park, runs north to the historic Clock Tower and former government buildings, and south into the neon buzz of Susukino, one of Japan’s great nightlife and dining districts. Add legendary food — miso ramen, soup curry, jingisukan and crab — plus year-round festivals, and Sapporo is the perfect base for exploring Hokkaido.

item.title: Sapporo Snow Festival Guide: Dates, Sites & Tips (Feb)
item.description: The Sapporo Snow Festival (Yuki Matsuri) is Japan’s biggest and most famous winter event, drawing millions to Hokkaido’s capital each February. For about a week, Odori Park becomes a glittering open-air gallery of colossal snow sculptures — towering castles, temples and pop-culture characters — alongside delicate ice sculptures in Susukino and a family snow-play zone at the Tsudome. After dark, the sculptures are spectacularly lit up and projection-mapped. With street food, hot drinks and a magical atmosphere, it’s a bucket-list winter experience.
